title_as_printed: Parkinson's disease mild cognitive impairment with MRI evidence of cholinergic nucleus 4 degeneration: A new subtype?

blind_codes.Sample_N: 162 PD-MCI (40 low Ch4 GMD + 122 normal Ch4 GMD); 171 PPMI healthy controls used only as norming reference

Task_Type.reason: The study defines a PD-MCI subtype by MRI Ch4 grey-matter density. It then compares clinical profile and time to cognitive-domain milestones between subtypes (Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, Cox HR). The progression outcome is the first-reached of six PPMI cognitive-domain milestones (p3: MoCA <21, MDS-UPDRS item 1.1 >=3, hallucinations, apathy, dementia diagnosis, dementia composite). That is neither progressive-vs-stable MCI labelling nor MCI-to-AD conversion, and no conversion-prediction model or discrimination figure is reported. The paper frames itself as subtyping ('A new subtype?'), which the template assigns to T4; T2 applies ONLY when the task is explicitly pMCI/sMCI or MCI-to-AD conversion.
Task_Type.quote: Objective: To determine whether PD-MCI patients with MRI evidence of Ch4 degeneration exhibit a different clinical profile and cognitive trajectory than those without Ch4 degeneration.

Category.reason: The primary domain is structural MRI (Ch4 GMD by voxel-based morphometry), which the registry carries. The clinical scales are the secondary C5 domain it omits: MDS-UPDRS, UPSIT, SCOPA-AUT, the neuropsychological battery and the PPMI milestones.
Category.quote: Those with low Ch4 GMD had significantly worse MDS-UPDRS total and subscale scores (II–III), greater autonomic dysfunction, and reduced olfaction (all P < 0.05).

Validation_Type.reason: No predictive model is validated: the analyses are group comparisons plus a survival association. The authors state that the threshold was derived and evaluated in the same cohort.
Validation_Type.quote: The Ch4 z-score threshold (−1 SD) was derived within the same cohort in which it was evaluated.

Sample_N_Approx.reason: 162 PD-MCI patients were analysed (122 normal + 40 low Ch4 GMD). The 171 PPMI healthy controls serve only as the norming reference.
Sample_N_Approx.quote: The sample size of 162 PD patients (n = 122 vs. 40)

ADNI_Dependent.reason: The data come from PPMI; ADNI is not used.
ADNI_Dependent.quote: using data from the Michael J. Fox Foundation’s Parkinson’s Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI)

notes: The T2 code puts this PD subtype study, which fits no classifier, into the review's T1-T3 classification subset. There it counts as a V2, non-ADNI classification study. The population is Parkinson's disease MCI (PD-MCI), not the AD continuum.
